steps.title: Prepare experimental recording room
steps.instruction: Select a chamber that can be darkened and shielded (ideally a Faraday cage) to control ambient light and electromagnetic noise while allowing air exchange. Line walls with non‑reflective black foam, curtains or paint (reflectance ≈0). Ensure vents remain unblocked, avoid fans, and monitor HVAC. Place a non‑swivel, black chair at the centre. Run all USB cables for PMTs and EEG from the centre to an external room via optically sealed conduits; label each cable. Install a low‑impedance grounding system with ground‑loop isolators or circuit breakers. Set up the required number of computers (e.g., separate laptops for EEG and PMT control).

steps.title: Configure EEG hardware
steps.instruction: Position the EEG digital amplifier box behind the chair and cover all external LEDs with black vinyl tape (verify darkness with a PMT). Choose a referential montage referenced to the ears (electrodes: Fp1, Fp2, F7, F3, Fz, F4, F8, T3, C3, Cz, C4, T4, T5, P3, Pz, P4, T6, O1, O2; references A1, A2; ground Az). Set sampling rate to 250 Hz, low‑cut filter 1.6 Hz, high‑cut filter 50 Hz, notch filters 50‑70 Hz and 110‑130 Hz, gain 100 µV. Connect a 19‑channel electro‑cap to the amplifier (keep electrode spacing sufficient for PMT line‑of‑sight).

steps.title: Prepare PMT system hardware
steps.instruction: Install flexible mounts (e.g., gooseneck phone‑holder clamps) around the chair. Insert PMTs into the mounts, orienting apertures toward the head. Use PMTs with spectral range 280–850 nm, dark counts ≈1000 photons s⁻¹, 22‑mm S20 cathode. Keep apertures closed (cover with opaque plastic) except during recording. Label each PMT and its USB cable (e.g., B‑PMT, O‑PMT, T‑PMT). Provide 5 V power supplies, routing power cables separately from EEG cables and avoiding bundling or twisting.

steps.title: Apply EEG cap and gel to participant
steps.instruction: Select cap size for head circumference, display cap, blunted syringes and gel to participant. Place cap on head and pull down firmly before plugging its cable into the amplifier. Fill each electrode hole with gel using the syringe, injecting while withdrawing to distribute evenly. Check impedance (WinEEG) – values <5 kΩ are acceptable; adjust gel if needed. Apply gel to ear‑clip electrodes (A1, A2, Az) and attach to ears (remove piercings). Record a short test segment to assess 60 Hz line noise, DC shifts or distortion; troubleshoot as required.

steps.title: Position and shield PMTs around head
steps.instruction: Clamp each PMT mount so the aperture is aimed at the head, positioned ≤5 cm from the scalp without touching hair or skin and without obstructing EEG electrodes. Keep the B‑PMT on the left side of the participant, aperture pointing away toward a wall. Ensure all PMTs are covered with opaque material when not recording and stored in anti‑static opaque bags. Verify consistent positioning across subjects.

steps.title: Initialize recording software
steps.instruction: Launch EEG acquisition software and set the same parameters as above (250 Hz, filters, gain). Launch the PMT counter‑timer software (e.g., Sense‑Tech). Set PMT sample rate to 25 Hz (40 ms intervals), high‑cut filter 30 Hz, notch filter 60‑120 Hz, gain 100 µV. Configure automatic termination after 15 000 measurements (≈10 min at 25 Hz).

steps.title: Dark‑adapt the recording environment
steps.instruction: Close all chamber doors and wait at least 5 minutes for ambient dark counts to stabilise before starting data acquisition.

steps.title: Record simultaneous EEG and UPE data
steps.instruction: Open PMT apertures, start both EEG and PMT recordings simultaneously, and let the system run until it automatically stops after 10 minutes (or 15 000 samples). Monitor signal quality throughout; pause if artefacts appear.

steps.title: Save raw data files
steps.instruction: Export EEG data and PMT photon‑count data to MATLAB‑compatible .mat files (e.g., UPEs.mat, EEG.mat) for subsequent analysis.

steps.title: Compute short‑FFT spectrograms
steps.instruction: Run ShortFFT_UPEs.m with parameters: filename='UPEs.mat'; fs=20 Hz; timeWindow=20 s; overlapLength=0.75; numSubjects=20. The script creates a Hann window of length timeWindow*fs, computes STFT, converts to power (dB), stores results in Spectrogram struct, and saves as Spectrogram.mat.

steps.title: Plot spectrograms
steps.instruction: Run Plot_spectrogram_UPEs.m with inputs: filename='Spectrogram.mat'; fs=20 Hz; timeWindow=20 s. Select desired electrode‑subject fields via list dialog, compute minimum frequency (1/timeWindow*2), and display each spectrogram using a jet colormap with colorbar labeled 'Power (dB)'.

steps.title: Perform pairwise correlation analysis
steps.instruction: Run ComputeCorrelationUPEs.mat supplying: filename (UPEs struct), ResampleFactor (1 = no resampling), cutoff (user‑defined), fs (sampling frequency), TimeWindow (seconds), Overlap (fraction), numSubjects (20). The script outputs NetworksCorrelation, NetworkEdgeTrajectories, and Corr structs containing median correlation values per electrode pair per subject.

steps.title: Perform pairwise coherence analysis
steps.instruction: Run ComputeCoherenceUPEs.mat with the same parameter set as the correlation step. The script outputs NetworksCoherence, NetworkEdgeTrajectories, and Coherence structs containing median coherence values per electrode pair per subject.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of metrics
steps.instruction: Run MixedEffectModels.R: 1) load libraries (readxl, lme4, lmerTest, tidyverse, car, emmeans); 2) import dataset from Excel (file_path); 3) fit linear mixed‑effects model with lmer (e.g., Dependent ~ Electrode*Task + (1|Subject) + (1|Subject:Electrode) + (1|Subject:Task) + (Task|Subject) + (Electrode|Subject)); 4) stop if model is singular; 5) print summary; 6) perform Type III ANOVA (Satterthwaite); 7) conduct Bonferroni‑adjusted pairwise post‑hoc tests for Electrode (and optionally Task|Electrode) using emmeans; 8) compute Cohen's d (estimate/σ_resid) and round all results; 9) output table with Task, contrast, estimate, SE, CI, t‑ratio, p‑value, Cohen’s d.
